guidebook.intro: Christians, Muslims and followers of other faiths live side by side in East Africa, and blessings are part of everyday speech.

tips.title: Being done to: -wa
body: Put **-w-** before the last **-a** and the verb becomes passive: **-ita** (call) → **-itwa** (be called), **-penda** → **-pendwa** (be loved), **-funga** → **-fungwa** (be closed, be beaten).
Some change a little more: **-zaa** (give birth) → **-zaliwa** (be born). **Alizaliwa** means “he or she was born”.

culture.title: Blessings everywhere
body: People say **Mungu akubariki** (God bless you), **Mungu akipenda** (God willing) and **Asante Mungu** (thank God) in everyday talk. During **Ramadhani**, many coastal towns go quiet by day and come alive after sunset.
